:::{#exm-diff-means-lincom}

#### Difference in mean birthweight as a linear combination

For the `birthweight` model with an interaction (`bw_lm2`),
let $\vx$ be the covariate pattern for males and $\vxs$ the pattern for females, both at 40 weeks.
The code below computes $\diffvx$,
and compares $\dprodf{\diffvx}{\evb}$ with the difference in the two predicted means:

```{r}
#| label: exm-diff-means-lincom-calc
ex_pair <- data.frame(
  sex = factor(c("female", "male"), levels = levels(bw$sex)),
  age = c(40, 40)
)
ex_design <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(bw_lm2)), ex_pair)
ex_delta_x <- ex_design[2, ] - ex_design[1, ]
ex_lincom <- sum(ex_delta_x * coef(bw_lm2))
ex_diff <- diff(predict(bw_lm2, newdata = ex_pair))
```

The linear combination is `r round(ex_lincom, 1)` grams,
and the difference in predicted means is `r round(ex_diff, 1)` grams,
so @thm-diff-means-lincom holds for the fitted coefficients.

:::
